Spacecraft and rockets by mass.Sputnik 1: The polished 58 cm sphere beeped over radio for about three weeks and kicked off the Space Age and the space race.
Spacecraft and rockets by mass.Sputnik 2 (with Laika): Laika, a Moscow street dog, became the first animal in orbit, but the craft had no return plan and she died within hours.
Spacecraft and rockets by mass.Voyager 1: Launched in 1977, it has been in interstellar space since 2012, the farthest human-made object, and still sends data home.
Spacecraft and rockets by mass.Cassini-Huygens (fueled): It orbited Saturn for 13 years, and its Huygens probe landed on Titan in 2005, the most distant landing yet made.
Spacecraft and rockets by mass.Hubble Space Telescope: Its main mirror was ground slightly wrong, so in 1993 astronauts installed corrective optics, like giving the telescope glasses.
Spacecraft and rockets by mass.Salyut 1: The first space station, launched in 1971. Its first crew died returning home when a valve opened and the cabin lost air.
Spacecraft and rockets by mass.Skylab: Built from a spare Saturn V stage, America's first station re-entered in 1979, scattering debris across Western Australia.
Spacecraft and rockets by mass.Mir: Mir stayed up for 15 years, and Valeri Polyakov lived aboard it for 437 days, still the longest single spaceflight.
Spacecraft and rockets by mass.International Space Station: People have lived aboard continuously since November 2000, and it is about as long as a football field.
Spacecraft and rockets by mass.Saturn V (fueled): Standing 110 m tall, it launched every crewed Moon mission, and its first stage burned most of the fuel in about two and a half minutes.

Bible figures, in story order.Adam: In Hebrew his name comes from the word for ground, adamah, and in effect means human, a word play in the Genesis story.
Bible figures, in story order.Noah: The flood story resembles older Mesopotamian tales such as Atrahasis and Gilgamesh, which scholars study as possible predecessors.
Bible figures, in story order.Abraham: Revered in Judaism, Christianity and Islam, he gives the Abrahamic religions their shared name.
Bible figures, in story order.Joseph and his coat: Sold into slavery by his brothers, he rose to be Egypt's chief minister, and the famous coat is often described as a richly ornamented tunic.
Bible figures, in story order.Moses: Led the Exodus out of Egypt, and his name sounds Egyptian, like pharaohs named Thutmose and Ramesses.
Bible figures, in story order.Samson: His strength was tied to his uncut hair, and he pulled down a temple on his Philistine enemies and himself.
Bible figures, in story order.King David: The shepherd boy who defeated Goliath with a sling became king, and tradition credits him with many of the Psalms.
Bible figures, in story order.Elijah: Said to have ascended in a whirlwind with a chariot of fire, he is honored at the Passover seder with a cup of wine set aside for him.
Bible figures, in story order.Daniel: Thrown into a den of lions in Babylon, he was famously unharmed, and his book is part of the Bible's apocalyptic tradition.
Bible figures, in story order.John the Baptist: He baptized Jesus in the Jordan River and lived in the wilderness, wearing camel hair and eating locusts and wild honey.

When the last native speaker of each lan.Cornish (Dolly Pentreath): Dolly Pentreath is traditionally called the last native Cornish speaker. The language has since been revived and is now taught to children in Cornwall.
When the last native speaker of each lan.Norn (Shetland): Norn grew from Old Norse and was spoken in Orkney and Shetland. Many of its words survive in Shetland dialect today.
When the last native speaker of each lan.Dalmatian: This Romance language of the Adriatic coast lost its last speaker, Tuone Udaina, who was killed in a blast while roadworks were under way.
When the last native speaker of each lan.Yahi (Ishi): Called 'the last wild Indian' in North America, Ishi walked out of the California foothills in 1911 and spent his last years at a university museum.
When the last native speaker of each lan.Manx (Ned Maddrell): Ned Maddrell's death ended the last unbroken line of native speakers on the Isle of Man, but recordings and schools have brought the language back.
When the last native speaker of each lan.Ubykh: Ubykh, once spoken on the Black Sea coast, had around 80 consonants but only two or three vowels. Tevfik Esenç, its last speaker, was recorded in detail.
When the last native speaker of each lan.Eyak (Alaska): Marie Smith Jones of Alaska spoke Eyak to the end and worked with linguists to record it. She also campaigned for Native cultures.
When the last native speaker of each lan.Bo (Andaman Islands): Boa Sr, last speaker of Bo, belonged to the Great Andamanese people, whose languages may descend from some of the oldest in the world.
When the last native speaker of each lan.Livonian: This small Finnic language was spoken on the coast of Latvia. Revival classes and songs are keeping it alive after its last native speaker died.
When the last native speaker of each lan.Klallam: Hazel Sampson was the last native speaker of Klallam in Washington State. Her tribe's Elwha language program now teaches new speakers.

How heavy is the brain?.Honeybee: A honeybee's brain has around a million neurons, yet bees can learn to recognize human faces and count small numbers.
How heavy is the brain?.House mouse: A mouse's brain holds about 70 million neurons, and mice are the most widely used animals in neuroscience.
How heavy is the brain?.Rat: Rats giggle in ultrasound when they play or are tickled, a laugh humans cannot hear, according to studies of rat emotions.
How heavy is the brain?.House cat: A cat has roughly 250 million neurons in its cerebral cortex, about half as many as a dog.
How heavy is the brain?.Beagle: Bred for scent, beagles have around 220 million smell receptors, compared with roughly 5 million in a person.
How heavy is the brain?.Chimpanzee: A chimp's brain is about a third the size of ours, even though we share around 98 percent of our DNA.
How heavy is the brain?.Horse: A horse's brain makes up barely 0.1 percent of its body weight, yet horses can read human facial expressions.
How heavy is the brain?.Human: The human brain is about 2 percent of body weight but uses roughly 20 percent of the body's energy.
How heavy is the brain?.African elephant: An elephant has about 250 billion neurons, around three times as many as a person, mostly in the cerebellum.
How heavy is the brain?.Sperm whale: The sperm whale has the biggest brain of any animal ever, around five times heavier than a human's.

When these treaties were signed.Peace of Augsburg: It let German princes choose Lutheran or Catholic for their lands, under the principle cuius regio, eius religio.
When these treaties were signed.Peace of Westphalia: Ending the Thirty Years' War, the peace treaties are credited with launching the modern idea of national sovereignty.
When these treaties were signed.Treaty of Utrecht: It ended the War of the Spanish Succession and gave Britain Gibraltar, which it still holds.
When these treaties were signed.Treaty of Paris (US): Britain recognized American independence in this treaty that ended the Revolutionary War.
When these treaties were signed.Congress of Vienna: Held after Napoleon's fall, it redrew Europe's map and set up a balance of power that kept the peace for decades.
When these treaties were signed.Treaty of Versailles: It was signed on June 28, five years to the day after Archduke Franz Ferdinand's assassination, in the Hall of Mirrors.
When these treaties were signed.Treaty of Rome (EEC): Six countries created what became the European Union, with the signing held on Rome's Capitoline Hill.
When these treaties were signed.Camp David Accords: After 13 days of talks hosted by Jimmy Carter, Egypt's Sadat and Israel's Begin made peace and shared a Nobel Peace Prize.
When these treaties were signed.Maastricht Treaty: It created the European Union and set the path to the euro.
When these treaties were signed.Treaty of Lisbon: It created a permanent EU Council president and introduced Article 50, the clause Britain later used to leave.

When these countries switched to the eur.Germany: Germany was a founding member in 1999, when the euro existed only electronically; notes and coins arrived in 2002.
When these countries switched to the eur.Greece: Greece joined in 2001, and its debt crisis from 2010 brought the euro's biggest scare, with talk of a Greek exit.
When these countries switched to the eur.Slovenia: Slovenia was the first ex-communist country to adopt the euro, and it held the EU's rotating presidency the very next year.
When these countries switched to the eur.Malta: Malta joined together with Cyprus in 2008, making it the smallest country in the eurozone by area at the time.
When these countries switched to the eur.Slovakia: Slovakia adopted the euro on 1 January 2009, in the middle of the global financial crisis, joining a tested currency.
When these countries switched to the eur.Estonia: Estonia was the first former Soviet republic to join the eurozone, after being one of the first countries to embrace digital government.
When these countries switched to the eur.Latvia: Latvia adopted the euro in 2014, and its one and two euro coins show a woman in national folk dress.
When these countries switched to the eur.Lithuania: Lithuania joined in 2015, and its coins feature Vytis, a knight on horseback that is the country's coat of arms.
When these countries switched to the eur.Croatia: Croatia joined the eurozone and the Schengen travel area on the same day, 1 January 2023, replacing the kuna.
When these countries switched to the eur.Bulgaria: On 1 January 2026 Bulgaria became the 21st country to adopt the euro, replacing the lev.

Weird things sent to space.Smuggled corned beef sandwich: Astronaut John Young smuggled it aboard Gemini 3; crumbs floated everywhere, and NASA was displeased enough that Congress asked questions.
Weird things sent to space.Golf balls hit on the Moon: Alan Shepard swung a makeshift club on Apollo 14, and in the Moon's weak gravity the shot flew far further than on Earth.
Weird things sent to space.Voyager Golden Record: This gold-plated disc carries greetings in 55 languages, music and sounds of Earth, and is now travelling through interstellar space.
Weird things sent to space.Coca-Cola space can: Coke and Pepsi both sent specially designed drink cans up on Challenger in 1985 to test whether fizzy drinks work in orbit.
Weird things sent to space.Pizza Hut pizza to the ISS: A Russian rocket delivered it as a marketing stunt, which made it the first pizza ever delivered to orbit.
Weird things sent to space.Clyde Tombaugh's ashes: The discoverer of Pluto rode out on New Horizons; the probe flew past his planet in 2015 carrying a small portion of his ashes.
Weird things sent to space.Luke Skywalker's lightsaber: A prop of the Star Wars hero's weapon flew on shuttle Discovery, lent by George Lucas, as part of a celebration of the franchise.
Weird things sent to space.Buzz Lightyear figure: The toy astronaut spent over a year on the ISS after launching in 2008, living up to his catchphrase 'To infinity and beyond'.
Weird things sent to space.Lego figures on Juno: Three aluminum figures of Galileo, Jupiter and Juno, built to survive space, ride on the probe heading for the planet.
Weird things sent to space.A Tesla Roadster: Elon Musk's own car launched as a test payload on the first Falcon Heavy, with a spacesuited dummy named Starman at the wheel.

From a blip to centuries: how long it pl.Napalm Death's You Suffer: Napalm Death's grindcore track is listed by Guinness as the shortest song ever, barely over a second long.
From a blip to centuries: how long it pl.John Cage's silent piece: John Cage's 1952 work asks performers to stay silent, so the piece is the ambient sound of the hall.
From a blip to centuries: how long it pl.Bohemian Rhapsody: Queen's 1975 single was so long that labels warned radio would not play it, but DJ Kenny Everett did anyway.
From a blip to centuries: how long it pl.Hey Jude: At over seven minutes, it was the longest number one single of its time, and its na-na-na coda lasts about four.
From a blip to centuries: how long it pl.Stairway to Heaven: It was never released as a single, yet became one of the most-requested songs in rock radio history.
From a blip to centuries: how long it pl.In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida: Iron Butterfly's track, with a long drum solo, is a psychedelic landmark, and its title was reportedly a slurred In the Garden of Eden.
From a blip to centuries: how long it pl.Thick as a Brick (album): Jethro Tull's album is one 43-minute song, meant as a parody of overblown progressive rock concept albums.
From a blip to centuries: how long it pl.Wagner's Ring cycle: Wagner spent about 26 years writing the four operas, and they are performed on four consecutive evenings.
From a blip to centuries: how long it pl.As Slow As Possible (organ): John Cage's organ piece is being played in a church in Halberstadt, Germany, starting in 2001 and scheduled to end in 2640.
From a blip to centuries: how long it pl.Longplayer: Jem Finer's piece for singing bowls began on 1 January 2000 and is meant to run on computers until the end of 2999.

Classic novels, by publication year.Don Quixote: Cervantes' tale of a delusional knight gave English the word 'quixotic', and it is often called the first modern novel.
Classic novels, by publication year.Robinson Crusoe: Defoe's castaway story was based partly on the real sailor Alexander Selkirk, and it appeared under the title page claiming to be a true autobiography.
Classic novels, by publication year.Gulliver's Travels: Swift's satire, of the voyages to Lilliput and beyond, was first published anonymously, and it was meant for adults though it became a children's classic.
Classic novels, by publication year.Pride and Prejudice: Austen's novel opens with one of literature's most famous lines about a single man with a good fortune, and was originally titled 'First Impressions'.
Classic novels, by publication year.Frankenstein: Mary Shelley began this at 18 during a ghost-story contest on Lake Geneva, and the creature in it is unnamed, with Frankenstein the scientist.
Classic novels, by publication year.Moby-Dick: Melville's novel sold poorly in his lifetime, and its opening line, 'Call me Ishmael', is one of the best known in American literature.
Classic novels, by publication year.War and Peace: Tolstoy's epic, of Russian families during Napoleon's invasion, has over 500 characters, and its length is around 1,200 pages.
Classic novels, by publication year.The Great Gatsby: Fitzgerald's Jazz Age novel sold modestly when it came out, and the green light at the end of Daisy's dock is its famous symbol.
Classic novels, by publication year.Nineteen Eighty-Four: Orwell's dystopia gave us 'Big Brother', 'doublethink' and 'Orwellian', and it was written on a remote Scottish island, Jura.
Classic novels, by publication year.Harry Potter (book 1): J.K. Rowling's first book was rejected by a dozen publishers before it was accepted, and its US edition was retitled 'Sorcerer's Stone'.

When these brain chemicals were discover.Acetylcholine: Acetylcholine was the first neurotransmitter ever identified, by Otto Loewi, who said the experiment came to him in a dream.
When these brain chemicals were discover.Substance P: Substance P is involved in pain signaling, and it was discovered when a powdered extract of gut tissue was found to make muscle contract.
When these brain chemicals were discover.Noradrenaline: Noradrenaline, also called norepinephrine, helps drive the fight-or-flight response and keeps you alert.
When these brain chemicals were discover.Serotonin: Serotonin was first found in blood and later in the brain, and most of the body's supply is actually made in the gut.
When these brain chemicals were discover.GABA: GABA is the brain's main inhibitory chemical, calming nerve activity, and it is the target of anti-anxiety drugs like benzodiazepines.
When these brain chemicals were discover.Dopamine (as a messenger): Arvid Carlsson showed dopamine is a messenger in its own right, work that led to levodopa treatment of Parkinson's disease and a Nobel Prize.
When these brain chemicals were discover.Endorphins: Endorphins were discovered while scientists searched for the body's own version of morphine, and the name comes from 'endogenous morphine'.
When these brain chemicals were discover.Nitric oxide (as a signal): Nitric oxide, a gas known as a pollutant, turned out to carry signals in the body, and it was named Molecule of the Year in 1992.
When these brain chemicals were discover.Anandamide: Anandamide was named after the Sanskrit word for bliss, and it is the body's own version of the active ingredient in cannabis.
When these brain chemicals were discover.Orexin: Orexin, discovered by two labs, regulates wakefulness, and its loss causes the sleep disorder narcolepsy.

How hot these things get.Home freezer: At -18 °C bacteria cannot grow, so frozen food stays safe indefinitely, though its quality fades with time.
How hot these things get.Refrigerator: Cold slows but does not stop everything: Listeria is one bacterium that can still grow, slowly, at fridge temperatures.
How hot these things get.Hot tub (max): Guidelines cap hot tubs near 40 °C because during a long soak your body temperature can climb to a dangerous level.
How hot these things get.Water heater setting: Around 60 °C stops Legionella bacteria from growing in the tank, yet water that hot can scald skin within seconds.
How hot these things get.Finnish sauna: Finland has roughly three million saunas for about 5.5 million people, so nearly every household has one.
How hot these things get.Clothes iron, linen setting: Linen takes the hottest iron setting because flax fibers tolerate heat well, while synthetics can melt under it.
How hot these things get.Self-cleaning oven cycle: The cycle, called pyrolytic cleaning, burns baked-on grime to loose ash that you simply wipe out, and the door locks while it runs.
How hot these things get.Candle flame: The yellow glow comes from tiny soot particles heated white-hot, while the dim blue base is where the wax burns most completely.
How hot these things get.Gas stove flame: A blue flame signals complete combustion; if it turns yellow and flickers, the burner is getting too little air.
How hot these things get.Light bulb filament: Tungsten melts at about 3,400 °C, the highest of any metal, which is why it was chosen to glow inside bulbs.

Great floods through history.Yellow River flood: The Yellow River is known as China's Sorrow, and this flood is believed to have killed a million people or more.
Great floods through history.Johnstown Flood: A failed dam owned by a private fishing club sent a wall of water through the Pennsylvania town, killing over 2,200.
Great floods through history.Great Mississippi Flood: It displaced roughly 700,000 people and prompted the Flood Control Act of 1928, giving the federal government a major role in flood control.
Great floods through history.China floods: It may be the deadliest natural disaster ever, with estimates of one to four million deaths from flooding and famine.
Great floods through history.North Sea flood: A storm surge broke the dikes in the Netherlands, killing over 1,800 people there and prompting the giant Delta Works.
Great floods through history.Florence's Arno flood: The Arno flooded Florence's museums and libraries, and volunteers nicknamed mud angels rescued books and artwork.
Great floods through history.Great Midwest Flood (US): The Mississippi and Missouri stayed high for months, causing some $15 billion in damage across the Midwest.
Great floods through history.Central European floods: The Elbe inundated Dresden and Prague's old town, causing damage that put it among Europe's costliest floods.
Great floods through history.Pakistan floods: About a fifth of the country was underwater, affecting some 20 million people.
Great floods through history.Germany's Ahr Valley floods: Heavy rain turned the little Ahr river into a torrent, part of a disaster that killed about 180 people across Germany.

British beer cask sizes.Pint: UK pubs serve pints of about 568 ml, while the US pint is smaller at about 473 ml.
British beer cask sizes.Gallon: The imperial gallon is about 4.55 liters, noticeably bigger than the US gallon of 3.79.
British beer cask sizes.Pin: It holds 36 pints, a convenient size for a small party or a quiet pub cellar.
British beer cask sizes.Firkin: The name comes from Middle Dutch for 'fourth', since it's a quarter of a barrel and holds 72 pints.
British beer cask sizes.Kilderkin: Its name comes from Middle Dutch, and it holds 144 imperial pints, twice a firkin.
British beer cask sizes.Barrel: A beer barrel is 36 imperial gallons, or 288 pints, while the US standard barrel is 31 US gallons.
British beer cask sizes.Hogshead: The word was used for casks of wine, sugar and tobacco as well, and sizes varied with the liquid.
British beer cask sizes.Puncheon: It holds 72 gallons, two-thirds of a butt, and was also used to age rum and whisky.
British beer cask sizes.Butt: It's the traditional cask for sherry, and sherry-seasoned butts give many Scotch whiskies their flavor.
British beer cask sizes.Tun: Holding 216 gallons, a tun gave its name to the 'ton', which began as a measure of wine-cask cargo.

Mexican states by area.Mexico City: Formally the Federal District until 2016, it then became a state-like entity of its own, now officially Ciudad de México.
Mexican states by area.Morelos: Known as the land of eternal spring for its mild climate, it was home to revolutionary Emiliano Zapata.
Mexican states by area.State of Mexico: The most populous state, it wraps around Mexico City and contains the pyramids of Teotihuacan.
Mexican states by area.Yucatán: Near its coast lies the Chicxulub crater from the asteroid that ended the dinosaurs, and its cenotes were sacred to the Maya.
Mexican states by area.Jalisco: Tequila originated here, in the town of Tequila, and mariachi music also comes from this state.
Mexican states by area.Oaxaca: Famous for its mole sauces and mezcal, it is home to 16 officially recognized Indigenous peoples.
Mexican states by area.Durango: Its desert landscapes have served as sets for Hollywood Westerns for decades.
Mexican states by area.Coahuila: Rich in fossils, including dinosaurs, its Cuatro Ciénegas basin shelters unique microbial life.
Mexican states by area.Sonora: It borders Arizona and gave its name to the Sonoran Desert, and is known for beef and carne asada.
Mexican states by area.Chihuahua: Mexico's largest state is home to Copper Canyon, and gave its name to the tiny Chihuahua dog.

Great comets by the year they dazzled.Ikeya-Seki: This sungrazer passed within a few hundred thousand kilometers of the Sun's surface in 1965 and was visible in daylight. It's among the brightest comets of the century.
Great comets by the year they dazzled.Kohoutek: The "Comet of the Century" was predicted to be bright but turned out disappointing. Skylab astronauts observed it from orbit.
Great comets by the year they dazzled.Comet West: A bright comet with a long tail in 1976 that broke into four pieces as it passed the Sun, and was easily visible in the dawn sky.
Great comets by the year they dazzled.Halley's last return: Seen in 1986, it returns about every 76 years, and the next visit is due in 2061. It was a poor show compared with earlier ones.
Great comets by the year they dazzled.Hyakutake: Passed close to Earth in 1996, with a long blue-green tail. Japanese amateur astronomer Yuji Hyakutake discovered it with binoculars.
Great comets by the year they dazzled.Hale-Bopp: Visible to the naked eye for over a year and a half, and one of the most widely seen comets in history. It was discovered by two US amateurs.
Great comets by the year they dazzled.Comet McNaught: Brightest comet in about 40 years, it was briefly visible in daylight in January 2007 and grew a huge fan-shaped tail, best seen from the Southern Hemisphere.
Great comets by the year they dazzled.Comet Lovejoy: Found by Australian amateur astronomer Terry Lovejoy, this comet survived a close brush with the Sun's corona and later grew a tail.
Great comets by the year they dazzled.Comet NEOWISE: Discovered by the NEOWISE space telescope in March 2020, this comet was visible from the Northern Hemisphere in July.
Great comets by the year they dazzled.Tsuchinshan-ATLAS: This comet is named for a Chinese observatory and the ATLAS survey, and appeared bright in October 2024 and will not return for tens of thousands of years.

How long these foods are, end to end.Quinoa seed: This grain-like seed is actually a relative of spinach and beets, and it was sacred to the Incas.
How long these foods are, end to end.Grain of rice: Rice feeds more than half the world, and a single plant can produce a few thousand grains.
How long these foods are, end to end.Coffee bean: A coffee bean is really a seed from inside a red fruit called a cherry.
How long these foods are, end to end.Baby carrot: Baby carrots are usually cut and shaped from larger carrots, not grown small.
How long these foods are, end to end.Cinnamon stick: Cinnamon sticks are the rolled-up inner bark of a tropical tree, and they curl as they dry.
How long these foods are, end to end.Banana: Bananas are berries in botanical terms, while strawberries are not.
How long these foods are, end to end.Uncooked spaghetti: Spaghetti's name comes from the Italian word for string, and it is usually sold in pasta around this length.
How long these foods are, end to end.Subway Footlong: The sandwich's name is trademarked, and Subway has been sued over whether its footlongs are actually 12 inches.
How long these foods are, end to end.Baguette: This French bread has its own rules: Paris law set its weight and the ingredients that can go in a traditional one.
How long these foods are, end to end.Sugarcane stalk: Sugarcane is a giant grass, and it supplies most of the world's sugar.

When these food mascots were born.The Quaker Oats man: The Quaker Oats man, from 1877, was one of the first trademarks registered in the US for a cereal.
When these food mascots were born.Mr. Peanut: Mr. Peanut was created by a schoolboy who won a contest, and his monocle and top hat were added by an artist.
When these food mascots were born.Jolly Green Giant: The Jolly Green Giant was originally a scary-looking brute, and he now stands in a Minnesota town.
When these food mascots were born.Snap, Crackle & Pop: The crackling trio was created for Kellogg's Rice Krispies, and the cereal really does make noise in milk.
When these food mascots were born.Elsie the Cow: Borden's cartoon cow became so popular that a real cow was brought to the 1939 World's Fair.
When these food mascots were born.Tony the Tiger: This tiger from Kellogg's Frosted Flakes says "They're grrreat!", and he was voiced for decades by Thurl Ravenscroft.
When these food mascots were born.Trix Rabbit: The rabbit's tagline is "Silly rabbit, Trix are for kids!", and he never gets to eat the cereal.
When these food mascots were born.Ronald McDonald: The clown was created for McDonald's, and he was first played on TV by Willard Scott.
When these food mascots were born.Pillsbury Doughboy: Poppin' Fresh giggles when his belly is poked, and he was created by an ad agency.
When these food mascots were born.Taco Bell chihuahua: The talking dog said "Yo quiero Taco Bell," and he was voiced by Carlos Alazraqui.

Events of the Trojan War, in story order.Judgment of Paris: Paris chose Aphrodite as fairest over Hera and Athena, and she promised him Helen in return.
Events of the Trojan War, in story order.Helen taken to Troy: Marlowe wrote of her 'the face that launched a thousand ships'; she was Menelaus's wife from Sparta.
Events of the Trojan War, in story order.Greek fleet gathers at Aulis: Homer lists over 1,000 ships in his catalogue of the Greek fleet.
Events of the Trojan War, in story order.Iphigenia sacrificed: Agamemnon sacrificed his own daughter to calm the winds, which led his wife to later kill him.
Events of the Trojan War, in story order.Achilles sulks in his tent: This is how the Iliad starts: Achilles' rage at Agamemnon, who took away his prize, Briseis.
Events of the Trojan War, in story order.Patroclus slain by Hector: He wore Achilles' armour, so Hector believed he had killed the great hero.
Events of the Trojan War, in story order.Achilles kills Hector: Achilles dragged Hector's body behind his chariot around the walls of Troy.
Events of the Trojan War, in story order.Priam ransoms Hector's body: The old king snuck into Achilles' tent to kiss the hands that killed his son; the Iliad ends with Hector's funeral.
Events of the Trojan War, in story order.Paris kills Achilles: In later tradition, an arrow guided by Apollo struck his one weak spot, giving us the phrase 'Achilles' heel'.
Events of the Trojan War, in story order.The wooden horse enters Troy: Told in Virgil's Aeneid and the Odyssey; the priest Laocoon's warning became 'beware Greeks bearing gifts'.

Species count: from one to thousands.Platypuses: The only egg-laying mammal with venom: males have a spur on the hind leg.
Species count: from one to thousands.Zebras: Plains, Grevy's and mountain zebras; every zebra's stripes are unique, and Grevy's is endangered.
Species count: from one to thousands.Rhinos: Black, white, Indian, Javan and Sumatran; Javan and Sumatran are critically endangered.
Species count: from one to thousands.Crocodilians: Crocodiles, alligators, caimans and gharials, the closest living relatives of birds.
Species count: from one to thousands.Wild cats: The domestic cat descended from the African wildcat, a small species of this group.
Species count: from one to thousands.Hummingbirds: Found only in the Americas, some can beat their wings around 80 times a second.
Species count: from one to thousands.Primates: Humans are one of them; Madagascar's lemurs exist nowhere else.
Species count: from one to thousands.Bats: About a fifth of all mammal species are bats, the only mammals that can truly fly.
Species count: from one to thousands.Rodents: Rodents are more than 40 percent of all mammal species.
Species count: from one to thousands.Snakes: Only a minority of these legless reptiles are dangerous to people.

Months of the ancient Athenian calendar.Hekatombaion: Means 'change of neighbours'; the name is tied to a festival of Apollo, and some say people moved house around then.
Months of the ancient Athenian calendar.Metageitnion: It began the new year around midsummer, and its name refers to the sacrifice of a hundred oxen.
Months of the ancient Athenian calendar.Boedromion: The secret Eleusinian Mysteries, a famed ancient initiation ritual, were celebrated in this month.
Months of the ancient Athenian calendar.Pyanepsion: Beans were boiled and offered to Apollo in its Pyanepsia festival, a harvest rite of the autumn.
Months of the ancient Athenian calendar.Poseideon: Named for Poseidon, it was sometimes repeated as an extra month to keep the calendar aligned with the seasons.
Months of the ancient Athenian calendar.Gamelion: The name comes from gamos, marriage, so it was a popular time for weddings in the winter.
Months of the ancient Athenian calendar.Anthesterion: The Anthesteria flower festival, in honour of Dionysus, opened the new wine of the year.
Months of the ancient Athenian calendar.Elaphebolion: The City Dionysia, with great drama contests where tragedies and comedies were staged, took place in this month.
Months of the ancient Athenian calendar.Thargelion: Socrates was traditionally said to have been born during this month, a time of spring purification festivals.
Months of the ancient Athenian calendar.Skirophorion: Its name comes from the parasols (skira) carried at a summer festival in honour of Athena.

The year behind famous eureka stories.Archimedes in the bath: The tale says he ran through the streets shouting 'Eureka!' after noticing displacement while testing a king's crown. It may well be embellished.
The year behind famous eureka stories.Newton's falling apple: Newton himself told the story, from the family farm where he had retreated during plague. Nobody mentions the apple hitting his head.
The year behind famous eureka stories.Franklin's kite in a storm: Franklin may never have been struck. His idea was that lightning is electricity, and French experimenters had already confirmed it.
The year behind famous eureka stories.Darwin's Galápagos visit: The famous finches weren't an instant revelation: he only realized they were related species after returning to England.
The year behind famous eureka stories.Mendeleev's table dream: He said he saw the periodic table in a dream, and left gaps for undiscovered elements, correctly predicting gallium and germanium.
The year behind famous eureka stories.Röntgen's glowing screen: Wilhelm Röntgen spotted an unexpected glow from a screen and discovered X-rays. He won the first Nobel Prize in Physics for it.
The year behind famous eureka stories.Fleming's moldy dish: Alexander Fleming returned from holiday to find mold killing the bacteria in a dish. Penicillin became the first major antibiotic.
The year behind famous eureka stories.De Mestral's burrs (Velcro): After an Alpine walk, Georges de Mestral studied burrs under a microscope. He patented his hook-and-loop fastener in 1955.
The year behind famous eureka stories.Spencer's melted chocolate: Radar engineer Percy Spencer noticed a candy bar melting near a magnetron, which led to the first microwave oven.
The year behind famous eureka stories.Fry's hymnal bookmark: Art Fry sang in a church choir, and his bookmarks kept falling out. Spencer Silver's weak glue became the Post-it Note.

Sparkle factor: how much gems bend light.Ice: Ice bends light less than glass does, which is why an ice cube looks plain beside crystal.
Sparkle factor: how much gems bend light.Opal: Its colour comes from tiny silica spheres, not pigment, and it contains up to around ten percent water. Most come from Australia.
Sparkle factor: how much gems bend light.Amethyst: This purple quartz's name comes from Greek for 'not intoxicated', as it was once believed to protect from drunkenness.
Sparkle factor: how much gems bend light.Emerald: Nearly all emeralds contain internal flaws, known in the trade as the 'jardin', or garden.
Sparkle factor: how much gems bend light.Topaz: Most blue topaz is actually colourless stone that has been irradiated and heated to turn it blue.
Sparkle factor: how much gems bend light.Peridot: It forms deep in the Earth and also turns up in meteorites and the green sand of some Hawaiian beaches.
Sparkle factor: how much gems bend light.Ruby: Rubies and sapphires are the same mineral, corundum. A trace of chromium turns it red.
Sparkle factor: how much gems bend light.Zircon: Zircon crystals from Australia, roughly 4.4 billion years old, are the oldest known pieces of Earth's crust.
Sparkle factor: how much gems bend light.Diamond: Its high bend of light lets a well-cut stone trap rays inside and send them back out through the top as flashes of fire.
Sparkle factor: how much gems bend light.Moissanite: Henri Moissan first found it in a meteor crater in Arizona, but nearly all of today's moissanite is made in labs.

Units of distance, from everyday to cosm.Kilometre: The metric unit is a thousand metres, and it is the base for all the other measures on this list.
Units of distance, from everyday to cosm.Mile: The unit of distance comes from the Roman 'mille passus', a thousand paces, and it was standardised in England in 1593.
Units of distance, from everyday to cosm.Earth's diameter: The planet's diameter is almost 12,742 km, and it is so close to a sphere that it is only about 43 km wider at the equator.
Units of distance, from everyday to cosm.Light-second: Light travels this far in just a second, and it takes just over a second to reach us from the Moon.
Units of distance, from everyday to cosm.Earth-Moon distance: The Moon is on average about this distance away, and it is moving away at about 3.8 centimetres per year.
Units of distance, from everyday to cosm.Light-minute: Light covers this distance in sixty seconds, and sunlight takes about eight of these minutes to reach us.
Units of distance, from everyday to cosm.Astronomical unit (AU): The distance from the Earth to the Sun is used as a measuring stick in the solar system, and it was first measured accurately in the 18th century.
Units of distance, from everyday to cosm.Light-hour: Light needs an hour to cover this, and Voyager 1 is currently over 20 light-hours away.
Units of distance, from everyday to cosm.Light-year: A light-year measures distance, not time, and the nearest star is about four of them away.
Units of distance, from everyday to cosm.Parsec: This unit is the distance at which one astronomical unit spans one arcsecond, and it is the favourite unit of professional astronomers.

When these countries legalized same-sex.Netherlands: Mayor Job Cohen married four couples at midnight on 1 April 2001 in Amsterdam, making this the first country to do so.
When these countries legalized same-sex.Belgium: It was the second country to open marriage to same-sex couples, just two years after its neighbour did.
When these countries legalized same-sex.Spain: It became one of the first Catholic-majority countries to do so, despite fierce opposition.
When these countries legalized same-sex.South Africa: It is still the only African country to have done so, since its constitution bans discrimination on sexual orientation.
When these countries legalized same-sex.Norway: Its law took effect in January 2009, among the first in the Nordic region.
When these countries legalized same-sex.Argentina: It was the first country in Latin America to allow it, after a vote in the Senate.
When these countries legalized same-sex.France: The slogan was mariage pour tous, marriage for everyone, and large protests marked the debate.
When these countries legalized same-sex.Ireland: It was the first country to approve it by popular vote, with around 62 percent in favour in 2015.
When these countries legalized same-sex.Germany: Parliament voted after Angela Merkel allowed members a free conscience vote.
When these countries legalized same-sex.Taiwan: The first place in Asia to legalise it, after a constitutional court ruling.

Impressionists and friends, by birth yea.Camille Pissarro: The group's elder statesman, Pissarro was the only artist who showed at all eight Impressionist exhibitions.
Impressionists and friends, by birth yea.Édouard Manet: His 1863 Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe scandalized Paris, and he influenced the Impressionists without joining their shows.
Impressionists and friends, by birth yea.Edgar Degas: He painted ballet dancers and racehorses, and he preferred indoor scenes to painting outdoors, despite being called an Impressionist.
Impressionists and friends, by birth yea.Paul Cézanne: Often called the father of modern art, he painted Mont Sainte-Victoire again and again, and Picasso admired him.
Impressionists and friends, by birth yea.Claude Monet: His painting Impression, Sunrise gave the movement its name, and he painted his water lily garden at Giverny.
Impressionists and friends, by birth yea.Pierre-Auguste Renoir: He painted Luncheon of the Boating Party, and he was known for glowing skin tones and happy scenes.
Impressionists and friends, by birth yea.Paul Gauguin: He left a stockbroker's job to paint, and traveled to Tahiti, where he made some of his best-known work.
Impressionists and friends, by birth yea.Vincent van Gogh: He sold only about one painting in his life, and made over 2,000 artworks in about a decade.
Impressionists and friends, by birth yea.Georges Seurat: The pointillist of A Sunday on La Grande Jatte built images from tiny dots of color, and died at 31.
Impressionists and friends, by birth yea.Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec: Barely over 1.5 meters tall, he painted Paris nightlife, including the Moulin Rouge, and made posters famous.

Iconic jersey numbers.Derek Jeter: The New York Yankees retired his number after he played all 20 seasons with them, and he was long their captain.
Iconic jersey numbers.Babe Ruth: Ruth wore it because he batted third; the Yankees introduced numbers in 1929 by batting order, and retired his in 1948.
Iconic jersey numbers.Lou Gehrig: In 1939, the Yankees honored him by retiring this number, the first ever retired in Major League Baseball.
Iconic jersey numbers.David Beckham at Man United: Worn at Manchester United before him by George Best, Eric Cantona and later Cristiano Ronaldo, the number has been a United legend's shirt.
Iconic jersey numbers.Pele: The Brazilian star won three World Cups, and the number became a symbol for a team's creative playmaker.
Iconic jersey numbers.Tom Brady: He won six Super Bowls with the Patriots, a seventh with Tampa Bay, and New England retired the number in 2024.
Iconic jersey numbers.Joe Montana (49ers): Montana won four Super Bowls with San Francisco, and the NFL called him "Joe Cool" for his calm in the final minutes.
Iconic jersey numbers.Michael Jordan (Bulls): He wore it through the Bulls' six championships, and wore 45 during a 1995 comeback, then returned to the old number.
Iconic jersey numbers.Jackie Robinson: Every April 15, all MLB players wear it to honor the player who broke baseball's color line in 1947, and it is retired across the league.
Iconic jersey numbers.Wayne Gretzky: The NHL retired it league-wide in 2000, so no player can wear it again, honoring the sport's top scorer ever.

UK coins (and two US ones) by diameter.5p: The smallest UK coin has been this size since 1990, and it is smaller than a US cent.
UK coins (and two US ones) by diameter.US cent: Abraham Lincoln appeared on it from 1909, making him the first real person on a regular US coin.
UK coins (and two US ones) by diameter.1p: Since 1992 it has been a steel core coated with copper, and magnets stick to it.
UK coins (and two US ones) by diameter.20p: This seven-sided coin, introduced in 1982, is an equilateral-curve heptagon.
UK coins (and two US ones) by diameter.£1 (12-sided): Introduced in 2017, it replaced the round pound and has a hidden latent image and a bimetallic design.
UK coins (and two US ones) by diameter.10p: It is the same size as the old two-shilling florin, which remained in circulation after decimalisation.
UK coins (and two US ones) by diameter.2p: It is bigger than the 5p though worth less, a legacy of the days when coins held metal worth their face value.
UK coins (and two US ones) by diameter.50p: Seven-sided like the 20p, it appeared in 1969 and has been the subject of dozens of commemorative designs.
UK coins (and two US ones) by diameter.£2: Some of these bimetallic coins have an edge inscribed 'Standing on the shoulders of giants', a nod to Newton.
UK coins (and two US ones) by diameter.US half dollar: Kennedy's portrait appeared in 1964, within months of his assassination.

The life of King David, in story order.Anointed by Samuel: The youngest of eight sons of Jesse of Bethlehem was a shepherd boy when the prophet chose him.
The life of King David, in story order.Plays the harp for Saul: He soothed the king's torment with music long before he ever wore a crown.
The life of King David, in story order.Slays Goliath: With a sling and a stone, he beat the giant Philistine champion, who stood about three metres tall in some versions.
The life of King David, in story order.Covenant with Jonathan: Saul's son became his closest friend, and they swore loyalty to each other.
The life of King David, in story order.Spares Saul in a cave: At En Gedi, he cut a corner off Saul's robe and chose not to harm him.
The life of King David, in story order.Crowned king of Judah: He ruled Judah from Hebron for seven years, before the northern tribes accepted him.
The life of King David, in story order.Brings the Ark to Jerusalem: David danced in front of the Ark as it entered the city, which became his capital.
The life of King David, in story order.Bathsheba: He arranged the death of Bathsheba's husband, Uriah, and the prophet Nathan rebuked him.
The life of King David, in story order.Absalom's revolt: His own son rebelled, and David mourned when Absalom was killed.
The life of King David, in story order.Solomon named his heir: On Bathsheba's urging, the aging king chose her son over his older rival Adonijah.

When these hormones were discovered.Adrenaline: Jokichi Takamine isolated it in Japan, and it was the first hormone to be purified.
When these hormones were discovered.Thyroxine: The Mayo Clinic chemist Edward Kendall isolated it from thyroid tissue, and it helps regulate metabolism.
When these hormones were discovered.Insulin: Banting and Best sold the patent to the University of Toronto for one dollar each, hoping it would be freely available.
When these hormones were discovered.Estrogen: Its name comes from 'oestrus', and the discovery came through hormone research in several labs.
When these hormones were discovered.Testosterone: The male hormone was isolated in 1935 and synthesised soon after, earning a Nobel Prize.
When these hormones were discovered.Cortisone (first patient): First given in 1948 to a woman with severe rheumatoid arthritis, it earned a Nobel Prize in 1950.
When these hormones were discovered.Oxytocin (synthesized): It was the first peptide hormone made in a lab, by Vincent du Vigneaud, who won a Nobel Prize for it.
When these hormones were discovered.Melatonin: Aaron Lerner isolated it from cow pineal glands, noting it lightened the skin of frogs.
When these hormones were discovered.Leptin: Jeffrey Friedman's team discovered it by studying obese mice, and it signals how much fat the body stores.
When these hormones were discovered.Ghrelin: Japanese scientists found it, naming it for growth hormone release, and it makes your stomach rumble.

Famous numbers from ancient history.Hills of Rome: The seven hills are the Palatine, Aventine, Capitoline, Quirinal, Viminal, Esquiline and Caelian.
Famous numbers from ancient history.Tablets of early Roman law: Rome's first written laws, around 450 BC, were displayed in the Forum so that citizens could know them.
Famous numbers from ancient history.Stab wounds on Julius Caesar: Suetonius counted 23 wounds, and a physician reportedly said only one was fatal.
Famous numbers from ancient history.Hannibal's Alpine elephants: Hannibal crossed the Alps in 218 BC, and few elephants survived the cold and the passes.
Famous numbers from ancient history.Colosseum opening-games days: Titus inaugurated the Colosseum in AD 80 with 100 days of games, according to Suetonius.
Famous numbers from ancient history.Spartans at Thermopylae: Leonidas held the pass in 480 BC with 300 Spartans and several thousand allies against a vast Persian army.
Famous numbers from ancient history.Steps on El Castillo: The Maya pyramid at Chichen Itza has 91 steps on each of four sides plus a top platform, matching the days in a year.
Famous numbers from ancient history.Terracotta warriors: Over 8,000 life-size soldiers guard the tomb of Qin Shi Huang, and no two faces are alike.
Famous numbers from ancient history.Xenophon's Greek mercenaries: The Ten Thousand were Greek mercenaries who fought their way home from Persia, shouting Thalatta, the sea, on seeing it.
Famous numbers from ancient history.Settlements in Domesday Book: William the Conqueror's survey of 1086 got its name because its verdicts were final, like Judgment Day.

Milestones of human spaceflight.Yuri Gagarin orbits Earth: Gagarin's single orbit on Vostok 1 lasted 108 minutes.
Milestones of human spaceflight.Alexei Leonov's spacewalk: His suit ballooned in vacuum, and he had to let some air out to fit back into the airlock.
Milestones of human spaceflight.Apollo-Soyuz handshake: The first joint US-Soviet mission saw the crews shake hands in orbit in July.
Milestones of human spaceflight.Remek: first non-US/Soviet: Vladimir Remek of Czechoslovakia flew to the Salyut 6 station, first from outside the two superpowers.
Milestones of human spaceflight.Rakesh Sharma, first Indian: Asked by Indira Gandhi how India looked from orbit, he replied with the line of a famous Urdu poem: better than all the world.
Milestones of human spaceflight.Toyohiro Akiyama, 1st Japanese: A television journalist flew to Mir on a trip paid for by his employer, TBS.
Milestones of human spaceflight.Polyakov's record stay begins: Valeri Polyakov spent 437 days aboard Mir, the longest single spaceflight ever.
Milestones of human spaceflight.Dennis Tito's tourist trip: The American businessman reportedly paid around $20 million for his Soyuz ride to the ISS.
Milestones of human spaceflight.Yang Liwei, first Chinese: Shenzhou 5 made China the third country to launch people into orbit on its own.
Milestones of human spaceflight.Inspiration4 civilian crew: An all-civilian crew of four orbited for three days aboard a SpaceX Dragon, raising money for St. Jude hospital.

How long these take to cook.Blanching spinach: Dunking greens briefly in boiling water, then ice, keeps them bright green.
How long these take to cook.Toast: Browning toast is the Maillard reaction, which also gives crusts and roasted coffee their flavor.
How long these take to cook.Soft-boiled egg: Slightly older eggs peel more easily than very fresh ones because the white's pH rises.
How long these take to cook.Spaghetti: Salting the water barely changes its boiling point; it is for flavor.
How long these take to cook.White rice: It is the staple food for about half the world's people.
How long these take to cook.Baked potato: Wrapping it in foil steams rather than bakes it, and the skin turns soft.
How long these take to cook.Whole roast chicken: The safe US internal temperature is 165 F, or 74 C, measured at the thickest part.
How long these take to cook.Thanksgiving turkey: Domestic turkeys can't fly, though wild turkeys can fly up to about 55 mph.
How long these take to cook.Smoked brisket: Pitmasters wait through the stall, when the meat's temperature plateaus because evaporation cools it.
How long these take to cook.Sous-vide short ribs: The French for under vacuum, it cooks sealed food in a precise low-temperature bath, popularized in the 1970s by Georges Pralus.

Web services from the dial-up days to no.Yahoo!: It began as 'Jerry and David's Guide to the World Wide Web', a directory made by two Stanford students.
Web services from the dial-up days to no.eBay: Founder Pierre Omidyar launched it as AuctionWeb; legend says the first item sold was a broken laser pointer for about $15.
Web services from the dial-up days to no.Hotmail: The name was chosen because its letters spell out HTML, the web's markup language; Microsoft bought it in 1997 for reportedly around $400 million.
Web services from the dial-up days to no.Napster: Teenager Shawn Fanning wrote it, and it reached tens of millions of users before court orders shut it down in 2001.
Web services from the dial-up days to no.Skype: Built by Estonian engineers, it was bought by Microsoft in 2011 for about $8.5 billion.
Web services from the dial-up days to no.Flickr: Co-founder Stewart Butterfield later created Slack; Flickr itself grew out of an abandoned online game project.
Web services from the dial-up days to no.Google Maps: It grew from a startup bought by Google in 2004, founded by Danish-born brothers Lars and Jens Rasmussen.
Web services from the dial-up days to no.Spotify: Founded in Stockholm, it launched as a legal answer to music piracy and grew into the world's largest music streaming service.
Web services from the dial-up days to no.Zoom: Founded by Eric Yuan, a former WebEx engineer, it went from about 10 million daily participants in 2019 to some 300 million in 2020.
Web services from the dial-up days to no.Wordle: Software engineer Josh Wardle made it as a gift for his partner, and the New York Times bought it in early 2022.

Inventions named after their creators.Shrapnel shell: Henry Shrapnel's exploding shell was designed to spray balls over troops; the name later came to mean any flying fragments.
Inventions named after their creators.Guillotine: Dr Joseph-Ignace Guillotin campaigned for a more humane execution method, did not invent it, and disliked the name.
Inventions named after their creators.Braille: Louis Braille, blind from age three, devised his dot system at only 15.
Inventions named after their creators.Morse code: Samuel Morse was also a painter, and sent 'What hath God wrought' by telegraph in 1844.
Inventions named after their creators.Saxophone: Adolphe Sax of Belgium patented the instrument, and he reportedly survived several accidents and poisonings.
Inventions named after their creators.Pasteurization: Louis Pasteur created it to stop wine spoiling, rather than milk, and it later made milk safer to drink.
Inventions named after their creators.Ferris wheel: George Ferris built his giant wheel for the 1893 Chicago World's Fair as an answer to the Eiffel Tower.
Inventions named after their creators.Zeppelin: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin's rigid airships first flew over Lake Constance, and his name became a synonym for airship.
Inventions named after their creators.Geiger counter: Hans Geiger developed it from work with Ernest Rutherford, and its clicking became the sound of radiation.
Inventions named after their creators.Jacuzzi whirlpool bath: Candido Jacuzzi's family first built a hydrotherapy pump to ease his young son's arthritis; the whirlpool bath for homes followed.

How many chromosomes?.Jack jumper ant (female): It is the lowest known, found in Australia: females have just one pair of chromosomes, the fewest in any animal.
How many chromosomes?.Fruit fly: Thomas Hunt Morgan used the fly to prove genes sit on chromosomes, and many scientists use it as a lab model.
How many chromosomes?.Honeybee (female): Males hatch from unfertilised eggs and have only 16, while females have 32.
How many chromosomes?.House cat: Tortoiseshell cats are almost always female because of how a cat's X chromosomes switch on and off.
How many chromosomes?.Human: Our second-largest chromosome is a fusion of two ancestral ape chromosomes, which is why we have one fewer pair than chimps.
How many chromosomes?.Chimpanzee: It has two more than a human, and our closest living relatives carry that number.
How many chromosomes?.Donkey: Cross it with a horse's 64 and you get a mule with an in-between number.
How many chromosomes?.Mule: Its odd number of chromosomes cannot pair evenly, which usually makes it sterile.
How many chromosomes?.Horse: Przewalski's horse has 66, yet it can still breed with domestic horses.
How many chromosomes?.Dog: Dogs, wolves and coyotes all share 78 chromosomes, many of them tiny, and can interbreed.

When these science words were coined.Cell: Robert Hooke coined the biological cell after seeing cork under a microscope, because the tiny chambers looked like monks' cells.
When these science words were coined.Scientist: William Whewell coined scientist because natural philosopher felt old-fashioned. Some critics at the time disliked the new word.
When these science words were coined.Dinosaur: Richard Owen coined Dinosauria, meaning terrible lizard, as a group name, and he later helped found London's Natural History Museum.
When these science words were coined.Ecology: Ernst Haeckel coined ecology from the Greek oikos, house, treating nature as one big household.
When these science words were coined.Gene: Wilhelm Johannsen coined the word gene, from the Greek for birth, years before anyone knew what genes were made of.
When these science words were coined.Vitamin: Casimir Funk named vitamines, for vital amines. The final e was dropped later because not all of them are amines.
When these science words were coined.Photon: Gilbert Lewis proposed the word photon, though it was Einstein who had shown light acts as particles, called quanta.
When these science words were coined.Big Bang: Astronomer Fred Hoyle used Big Bang on BBC radio. He disliked the theory, though the name stuck anyway.
When these science words were coined.Quark: Murray Gell-Mann borrowed quark from James Joyce's Finnegans Wake, where seagulls cry Three quarks for Muster Mark.
When these science words were coined.Meme: Richard Dawkins coined meme in The Selfish Gene, modeling it on gene, as a unit of culture that copies itself.

Each country's highest point.Ireland: Carrauntoohil in Kerry is Ireland's highest peak, and it stands in the Macgillycuddy's Reeks range.
Each country's highest point.United Kingdom: Ben Nevis in Scotland is the highest mountain in the British Isles, and its summit is often in cloud.
Each country's highest point.Australia (mainland): Mount Kosciuszko was named by a Polish explorer after a Polish national hero, and it's in the Snowy Mountains.
Each country's highest point.Japan: Mount Fuji is a near-perfect volcanic cone, and it last erupted in 1707.
Each country's highest point.France: Mont Blanc is the highest peak in the Alps, and the first ascent in 1786 started the sport of mountaineering.
Each country's highest point.Russia: Mount Elbrus is in the Caucasus, and it's an extinct volcano often counted as Europe's highest peak.
Each country's highest point.Tanzania: Kilimanjaro is Africa's tallest mountain, and it's a freestanding volcano whose glaciers are fast shrinking.
Each country's highest point.United States: Denali in Alaska was officially renamed in 2015, from Mount McKinley, and its name means the high one.
Each country's highest point.Argentina: Aconcagua is the highest peak outside Asia, and it doesn't need technical climbing skill by the normal route.
Each country's highest point.Nepal: Everest is called Sagarmatha in Nepali, and Chomolungma in Tibetan, and it grows slowly by a few millimeters each year.

When colonial rule ended in these places.Philippines: It became independent from the US on July 4, 1946, after the Second World War.
When colonial rule ended in these places.Indonesia: The Dutch recognized it in 1949, after a four-year struggle that followed its 1945 proclamation.
When colonial rule ended in these places.Morocco: It became independent from France in March 1956, and Spain gave up its northern protectorate soon after.
When colonial rule ended in these places.Goa: India took it from Portugal in 1961 after 450 years of rule.
When colonial rule ended in these places.Aden: The British left in 1967 after an insurgency, and it became part of South Yemen.
When colonial rule ended in these places.Mozambique: The Carnation Revolution of 1974 in Portugal brought independence soon afterward.
When colonial rule ended in these places.Vanuatu: Once the New Hebrides, it was jointly ruled by Britain and France.
When colonial rule ended in these places.Hong Kong: Britain handed it back to China on July 1, 1997, under 'one country, two systems'.
When colonial rule ended in these places.Macau: Portugal's last overseas territory, handed over in December 1999.
When colonial rule ended in these places.East Timor: It became the first new sovereign state of the 21st century.

Melting points of everyday stuff.Olive oil: It turns cloudy and solid in a cold fridge, and it's still perfectly good once it warms.
Melting points of everyday stuff.Ice: It sets the zero of the Celsius scale at normal pressure, and salt lowers its melting point.
Melting points of everyday stuff.Coconut oil: It is solid in cool kitchens and liquid in warm ones, because its melting point is around room temperature.
Melting points of everyday stuff.Candle wax (paraffin): A petroleum byproduct, and the wick actually burns vaporized wax, not the solid.
Melting points of everyday stuff.Table sugar: It doesn't cleanly melt, but starts breaking down and caramelizing around this temperature.
Melting points of everyday stuff.Tin: Its low melting point made it ideal for solder, and bending a bar produces an audible 'tin cry'.
Melting points of everyday stuff.Table salt: Its high melting point is why road salt only helps by lowering ice's, not by melting itself.
Melting points of everyday stuff.Copper: People first smelted it about 7,000 years ago, one of the first metals ever worked.
Melting points of everyday stuff.Platinum: The international standard kilogram was made of a platinum-iridium alloy until 2019.
Melting points of everyday stuff.Tungsten: This has the highest melting point of any metal, which is why it was used for bulb filaments.

Classic songs by length.Yesterday - The Beatles: The melody came to Paul McCartney in a dream, and he first used the working title 'Scrambled Eggs'.
Classic songs by length.Love Me Do - The Beatles: The 1962 debut single had its drum track redone by session drummer Andy White on some versions.
Classic songs by length.Imagine - John Lennon: John Lennon's 1971 hit has had Yoko Ono listed as co-writer since 2017.
Classic songs by length.Billie Jean: Michael Jackson debuted the moonwalk performing it on Motown 25 in 1983.
Classic songs by length.Bohemian Rhapsody: The label thought it too long for radio, until DJ Kenny Everett played it repeatedly.
Classic songs by length.Like a Rolling Stone: At over six minutes it broke the single's length norms, and Rolling Stone later ranked it number one on its 500 list.
Classic songs by length.Hey Jude: Its final 'na na na' coda lasts over four minutes, longer than many entire songs.
Classic songs by length.Stairway to Heaven: Despite its fame, it was never released as a single in the US.
Classic songs by length.American Pie: It's about the 1959 plane crash that killed Buddy Holly, 'the day the music died'.
Classic songs by length.In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida: The title was supposedly a slurred version of 'In the Garden of Eden'.

When these constructed languages were cr.Lingua Ignota (Hildegard): The abbess of Bingen invented some 1,000 words and an alphabet, and nobody knows what for.
When these constructed languages were cr.Volapük: A German priest created it in 1879, and its name means 'world speech'.
When these constructed languages were cr.Esperanto: The name comes from the pen name Doktoro Esperanto, meaning 'one who hopes'.
When these constructed languages were cr.Tolkien's Quenya: Tolkien said his stories grew out of his invented languages, not the other way around.
When these constructed languages were cr.Interlingua: Its vocabulary was drawn from shared Romance language roots, so many people can read it unaided.
When these constructed languages were cr.Klingon: Marc Okrand created it for Star Trek III, and it has its own institute and Shakespeare translations.
When these constructed languages were cr.Lojban: It was built from logic, to avoid ambiguity, in a line from Loglan.
When these constructed languages were cr.Toki Pona: Sonja Lang built it with only about 120 to 140 words.
When these constructed languages were cr.Na'vi (Avatar): Linguist Paul Frommer built it at USC with over a thousand words for the film.
When these constructed languages were cr.Dothraki (on TV): David J. Peterson built it for Game of Thrones, and also built Valyrian.

Thanksgiving Parade balloons, by debut.Felix the Cat: Debuting in 1927, the first character balloon was a silent film star, and the parade's balloons were once released into the sky afterward.
Thanksgiving Parade balloons, by debut.Mickey Mouse: Mickey's balloon first appeared in the parade in 1934, six years after the mouse debuted in Steamboat Willie.
Thanksgiving Parade balloons, by debut.Popeye: The sailor man's balloon joined the lineup in 1957, a time when Popeye was a huge hit on TV cartoons.
Thanksgiving Parade balloons, by debut.Snoopy: Charles Schulz's beagle has appeared in the parade in more forms than any other character, including as a flying ace.
Thanksgiving Parade balloons, by debut.Kermit the Frog: Jim Henson's Muppet star appeared in a balloon in 1977, a year after The Muppet Show premiered.
Thanksgiving Parade balloons, by debut.Garfield: The orange cat's first balloon came in 1984, and he's known for hating Mondays and loving lasagna.
Thanksgiving Parade balloons, by debut.Spider-Man: The web-slinger debuted in the parade in 1987, and his balloon has been re-designed several times since.
